en: May the many-invoked, powerful lion protect us— his long, sharp claws having torn asunder the enemy’s host of intoxicated elephants,
each of whom acted like an individual thunderbolt,
and who were split apart at a great distance by those claws that were more capable than mountains in shattering lofty peaks.
With minds purified by vast portions of merit, they have meditated upon that which has utterly destroyed darkness and is perfectly tranquil.
Even when searching everywhere for anything equal to the Beloved of Lakṣmī,
I do not see anything equal to the Lord; I perceive only the eighth flavor (the marvelous) cast far away,
which is like a flickering fire rising from the tip of the curved right eye of Śiva, who is a mass of intense brilliance.
The heaps of Brahmā, Īśvara, and Śakra are like sparks resembling fireflies, reduced to ashes. || 2 ||
Thus ends the *Śrī Nṛsiṃhanakhastuti*, composed by the venerable teacher Śrīmad Ānandatīrtha Bhagavatpādācārya.
May this be offered unto Śrī Kṛṣṇa, who resides within the Chief Vital Breath (Mukhyaprāṇa) and the Delight of Sarasvatī (Bhāratīramaṇa).
